title: Phantom Protocol (OTel)
description: Phantom Protocol observability dashboard, Phase 8 OTel-native metric names. Pairs with docs/observability/prometheus/alerts.yml.

panels.title: Active streams
panels.description: User-visible streams currently open, from the balanced per-session StreamGauge (api/session.rs). Reserved stream ids 0 (control) and 1 (raw-app default) are excluded, and the gauge drains at session teardown, so it returns to zero. Unlabeled by design — stream_id is never a metric attribute.

panels.title: Cookie outcomes / sec
panels.description: Stateless-cookie address-validation events, recorded by udp_admit (the UDP demux pre-gate) and cookie_pow_gate in transport/handshake.rs. validated_ok / validated_mismatch come from a cookie the client actually presented; issued comes from the retry path. A hello with no cookie is not a validation event.

panels.title: PoW outcomes / sec
panels.description: Proof-of-work DoS-gate outcomes, recorded by cookie_pow_gate in transport/handshake.rs when the per-IP adaptive difficulty is above zero. Only a solution the client actually presented is counted (solved / rejected); a hello with no solution just gets a challenge issued, so first contact does not inflate the rejection rate. The PhantomPoWRejectionStorm alert reads this same series.

panels.title: Early-data outcomes / sec
panels.description: 0-RTT early-data outcomes, recorded by process_client_hello (transport/handshake.rs) once per hello that carried a sealed blob: accepted, rejected_unknown_ticket, rejected_oversized, rejected_aead, rejected_replay, rejected_disabled. A hello that offers no blob is not a 0-RTT decision and emits nothing, so this panel is blank only when no client is offering early data. rejected_disabled is the A2b operator kill switch (set_early_data_enabled(false)) — checked before any ticket lookup or AEAD work, so a disabled server never mis-attributes a blob to a client-side cause. If the whole panel is flat, check rejected_disabled before concluding that no client wants 0-RTT.

panels.title: Path migrations / sec
panels.description: Connection-migration events, recorded at four call sites in api/session.rs: the client Migrate command, the MigrateServer command, peer-migration detection on an authenticated forward path_id, and the M-3 passive NAT-rebind promotion. to_path 1..=254 is an active migration (the id wraps 254 to 1, skipping 0 and 255); to_path 255 is the reserved rebind-validation id and marks a passive NAT rebind.

panels.title: Path RTT (μs) by path_id
panels.description: Latest observed RTT per path, recorded by feed_bbr_on_ack (api/session.rs) from the authenticated-SACK path. Karn-gated: an ACK for a retransmit is not sampled, and a zero-microsecond sample is skipped. The label is the inbound header.path_id, so it stays 0 until the peer migrates; only slots 0..=15 are stored (MAX_PATHS = 16) and only paths with a non-zero last sample are observed.

panels.title: Path validation outcomes / sec
panels.description: PATH_CHALLENGE resolutions, one sample per issued challenge. success/failure come from handle_packet's PATH_VALIDATION arm when the peer answers; timeout comes from the pump's heartbeat sweep (sweep_path_validation_timeouts in api/session.rs) when it never does. Read them differently: a failure is a wrong echo from something that holds the session key, a timeout is a path carrying nothing at all (blackholed migration, NAT never opened, peer gone). The timeout budget is the session's own path-down threshold — path_down_ptos x max(min_pto, 3 x min_rtt) from LivenessConfig — so it scales with the measured RTT. The sweep is metrics-only: it does not move the path registry out of Validating. path_id 255 is the reserved M-3 passive-rebind validation id; 1..=254 are active migrations.
